psi.title: ID-PMC Psychological Safety Index — PSI
psi.objective: Measure how far team members can speak up, learn, contribute and challenge without fear of being humiliated, marginalised or penalised.
psi.quote: Psychological safety is not the freedom to say anything. It is the ability to say what needs to be said, respectfully, when collective performance requires it.
psi.question: To what extent do the following statements match what you actually experience in your team?
psi.scale: 1 = Strongly disagree · 2 = Somewhat disagree · 3 = Mixed · 4 = Somewhat agree · 5 = Strongly agree

dimensionTitle.contributing: Contributing, taking initiative and using one's abilities
dimensionTitle.challenging: Challenging, telling the truth and questioning the status quo

dimensionQuestion.belonging: Can I be a full member of this team without having to conform or fear being marginalised?
dimensionQuestion.learning: Can I show that I don't know without losing credibility?
dimensionQuestion.contributing: Can I really bring what I can do and take initiative?
dimensionQuestion.challenging: Can I say what I think when what I think is uncomfortable?

statements: I feel respected and considered a full member of this team, regardless of my role, seniority or status.
Differences in personality, background, culture, working style or point of view are genuinely accepted in this team.
I am involved in the discussions and decisions concerning my scope, and I do not feel deliberately kept out.
I can ask a question, request clarification or admit I do not master a topic without fear of being seen as incompetent.
I can openly acknowledge a mistake or a bad decision without fear that it will later be used against me.
When something does not work, we first seek to understand and learn before looking for someone to blame.
My ideas, proposals and contributions are listened to and considered, even when they are ultimately not adopted.
I have enough autonomy to take initiative and solve problems within my level of responsibility.
The leader deliberately creates opportunities for everyone to contribute, including those who speak up less spontaneously.
I can openly express disagreement with a decision, even when it is backed by my superior or someone more influential than me.
I can report a risk, bad news or an important problem even when the message is likely to be unwelcome.
In this team, questioning an old way of doing things or proposing a radically different approach is encouraged when it can improve performance.
